advisories.reason: Unauthenticated manual mock registration interpolates unescaped URLs into generated modules on the Vitest Vite development server (moderate). Fixed in Vitest 4.1.12 and 5.0.3; RITEway 9.3.0 requires Vitest ^3.2.4.

Tests use riteway/bun backed by bun:test. Production package absence is not assumed.

advisories.dependencyPath: workspace:@daisy/admin > riteway 9.3.0 (devDependency) > glob 11.1.0; workspace:@daisy/realtime > @sentry/bun > @sentry/bundler-plugins > glob 13.0.6; workspace:@daisy/web > @sentry/nextjs > @sentry/bundler-plugins > glob 13.0.6; a further glob 7.2.3 sits under the same lint/test tooling.
advisories.reason: AbortSignal cancellation bypass allows post-timeout filesystem traversal (moderate). Every glob from 9.0.0 through 14.0.1 is affected, so no in-range bump of riteway or @sentry/bundler-plugins clears it.
advisories.unreachable: Physically present in production installs via @sentry/nextjs > @sentry/bundler-plugins, but never executed there: bundler-plugins requires glob in exactly one module (build/cjs/core/glob.js), imported only by its rollup plugin, and @sentry/nextjs loads bundler-plugins only from its webpack config and build hooks - every call runs inside the `next build` process over repository files. @sentry/bun's runtime entrypoints (index, sdk, client) never require its bundler plugin. The prod-deps image stage installs without devDependencies, so the riteway/eslint chains are absent; the traversal finding additionally needs an AbortSignal-timed glob over attacker-chosen paths, which no build performs. (ADR 0093)

advisories.dependencyPath: eslint > @eslint/eslintrc > minimatch 3.1.5; typescript-eslint > @typescript-eslint/utils > @typescript-eslint/typescript-estree > minimatch 10.2.6; eslint-config-next > eslint-plugin-react > minimatch; riteway > glob > minimatch; @sentry/bundler-plugins > glob > minimatch.
advisories.reason: Denial of service via glob-part amplification (moderate). Everything below minimatch 11.0.1 is affected, and the lint ecosystem pins 3.x and 10.x ranges.
advisories.unreachable: minimatch rides into production installs only through glob (above) and the dev-only lint chains; with glob never required at runtime, minimatch never executes there either. The amplification finding requires an attacker-controlled glob pattern string; no production path passes one, and the lint tools that could only ever run on Daisy's own files in CI. (ADR 0093)

advisories.dependencyPath: workspace:@daisy/web > @sentry/nextjs 11.10.0 > @rollup/plugin-commonjs 28.0.1 (and its @rollup/pluginutils 5.5.1) > picomatch 4.0.7; knip 6.37.0 (dev) > picomatch / fdir 6.5.0 > picomatch 4.0.7; typescript-eslint 8.70.0 and eslint-config-next 16.3.5 (eslint-import-resolver-typescript) > tinyglobby 0.2.17 > fdir > picomatch 4.0.7; riteway 9.3.0 (dev) and better-auth's optional vitest peer > vitest 3.2.7 > vite 7.3.7 / tinyglobby > picomatch 4.0.7; eslint-config-next > @next/eslint-plugin-next > fast-glob 3.3.1 > micromatch 4.0.8 > picomatch 2.3.2.
advisories.reason: ReDoS through single-branch repeated extglobs (high). Every picomatch through 4.0.7 is affected and no patched release exists.
advisories.unreachable: Physically present in production installs via @sentry/nextjs > @rollup/plugin-commonjs, but never executed there: @sentry/nextjs requires plugin-commonjs only in build/cjs/config/loaders/wrappingLoader.js, a webpack loader that runs inside `next build`. The remaining chains are lint, test and knip tooling (eslint, typescript-eslint, knip, vitest/vite, fast-glob) over repository-authored globs. No apps/* or packages/* source imports picomatch, micromatch, tinyglobby, fdir, fast-glob, vite or @rollup/*; a production `next build` of apps/web traces none of them into any of its 225 server .nft.json files, and the other services run from source on Bun with no such import. The only picomatch in the web and admin Next servers is Next's vendored next/dist/compiled/picomatch (not this lockfile package), used for images.localPatterns/remotePatterns, which both apps leave at the framework default `**` - no extglob. The finding needs an attacker-chosen pattern; none reaches any matcher.
